thread.title: Apple Warns Employees once again to Stop Leaking Information

author: Jack Purcher
title: Apple Warns Employees once again to Stop Leaking Information

organizations.name: stop leaking information apple warns employees

text: Apple Warns Employees once again to Stop Leaking Information A new report today claims that Apple has warned employees to stop leaking internal information on future plans and raised the specter of potential legal action and criminal charges, one of the most-aggressive moves by the world's largest technology company to control information about its activities. Apple said in a lengthy memo posted to its internal blog that it "caught 29 leakers," last year and noted that 12 of those were arrested . "These people not only lose their jobs, they can face extreme difficulty finding employment elsewhere," Apple added. Apple outlined situations in which information was leaked to the media, including a meeting earlier this year where Apple's software engineering head Craig Federighi told employees that some planned iPhone software features would be delayed . Apple also cited a yet-to-be-released software package that revealed details about the unreleased iPhone X and new Apple Watch. Leaked information about a new product can negatively impact sales of current models, give rivals more time to begin on a competitive response, and lead to fewer sales when the new product launches, according to the memo. "We want the chance to tell our customers why the product is great, and not have that done poorly by someone else," Greg Joswiak, an Apple product marketing executive, said in the memo. For more on this, read the full Detroit News report here . It makes you question, who leaked this latest memo on leakers? Apple or an evil leaker? Last year Patently Apple posted a report titled " Apple has begun a new War on Leakers telling Staff that When they Leak Information, they're letting Everyone Down ," which mirrored this recent memo. I remember Apple Firing an Engineer over his Daughter's innocent iPhone X Video later in the year. We had learned that there could be an alien head Animoji in the works. Big deal. But that's not really a classic "leaker" case. It seems that Axios and Bloomberg constantly get the big "leaks." Until that level of leaker is caught, it's hard to take Apple's memos on this topic seriously. On the flip side, rumors get Apple a ton of free publicity which fires up the brokers selling AAPL stock. Hot rumors race around the globe and more than likely Apple is getting credit for things that they're not even working on. So there's some pluses to product or service rumors. Though I must admit, Apple events have been deadly boring for years mainly due to everything debuting being known weeks and months ahead of time. Apple's move into augmented reality last year was the first thing in some time that was actually fresh. I think we'd all like to be more surprised while watching live events. Perhaps Apple will get there some day if they're serious about pressing legal action against internal leakers. Of course the first test will be related to Apple's World Wide Developer Conference coming up in June. Will the leakers go silent? I rather doubt it, but time will tell.   our Site:   any comments.
